chapters.title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Head and Neck: Soft Tissues, Fascial Planes and Airway
chapters.description: Structural anatomy and functional relationships of the head and neck relevant to swelling, infection, airway compromise and dysphagia.
subtopics: Superficial and deep cervical fascia and compartments (pretracheal, retropharyngeal, parapharyngeal spaces)
Strap muscles, suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles, and their relationships to neck soft tissue swelling
Pharynx, larynx and upper airway anatomy (vallecula, pyriform fossa, vocal cords, epiglottis)
Salivary glands and ducts (submandibular, sublingual, parotid)
Neurovascular structures (cranial nerves IX–XII, cervical plexus, carotid sheath contents)
Lymphatic drainage of head and neck
Anatomy relevant to endoscopy, surgical access and airway management

chapters.title: Swallowing Physiology and Dysphagia: Mechanisms and Assessment
chapters.description: Normal swallowing mechanisms, causes of oropharyngeal dysphagia and diagnostic evaluation methods.
subtopics: Phases of swallowing (oral preparatory, oral transit, pharyngeal, esophageal)
Muscles and neural control of swallowing
Mechanisms of aspiration and penetration
Clinical features distinguishing oropharyngeal vs esophageal dysphagia
Instrumental assessments (video fluoroscopic swallow study / modified barium swallow, fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing)
Management principles (diet modification, enteral feeding options, swallowing rehabilitation)
Complications of dysphagia (aspiration pneumonitis, malnutrition, airway compromise)

chapters.title: Skeletal Muscle Structure, Function and Biomarkers
chapters.description: Skeletal muscle histology and physiology, mechanisms of muscle injury and the laboratory markers used to detect myocyte damage.
subtopics: Muscle fiber types, fascicular organization, connective tissue (endomysium, perimysium, epimysium)
Mechanisms of muscle injury and regeneration
Creatine kinase (isoforms), lactate dehydrogenase, aldolase and transaminases as muscle injury markers
Urine myoglobin and risk of myoglobinuria/acute kidney injury
Electromyography basics for myopathy vs neuropathy
MRI and PET imaging appearances of active myositis vs chronic changes

chapters.title: Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies: Clinical Features and Classification
chapters.description: Spectrum of inflammatory myopathies (including dermatomyositis, polymyositis, immune-mediated necrotising myopathy, inclusion body myositis) and their typical clinical presentations.
subtopics: Definitions and classification criteria for dermatomyositis and other idiopathic inflammatory myopathies
Epidemiology, age distribution and typical disease courses
Cutaneous manifestations associated with dermatomyositis (heliotrope, Gottron papules, shawl/V-neck sign, Holster sign, periungual changes)
Muscle involvement patterns (proximal weakness, respiratory and bulbar muscle involvement, dysphagia)
Extra-muscular manifestations (interstitial lung disease, cardiac involvement, arthritis, systemic features)
Severity assessment and disease activity indices

chapters.title: Dermatomyositis Pathophysiology: Immune Mechanisms and Microvascular Injury
chapters.description: Underlying immunopathology of dermatomyositis, including complement-mediated microangiopathy, interferon pathways and consequences for skin and muscle.
subtopics: Humoral and complement-mediated mechanisms (capillary injury, C5b-9 membrane attack complex deposition)
Type I interferon signature and downstream inflammatory cascades
Perifascicular atrophy and selective fiber injury
Mechanisms of subcutaneous edema in inflammatory myopathies
Relationship between autoantibodies and pathogenic pathways
Overlap syndromes and secondary organ involvement (lung, GI tract, heart)

chapters.title: Myositis-Specific and Myositis-Associated Autoantibodies: Testing and Clinical Associations
chapters.description: Major autoantibodies in inflammatory myopathies, the laboratory methods to detect them, and their clinicopathologic correlations (including cancer risk and ILD associations).
subtopics: Common myositis-specific antibodies (anti-Jo-1, anti-PL-7, anti-PL-12, anti-Mi-2, anti-MDA5, anti-TIF1-γ, anti-SAE1) and their phenotype associations
Myositis-associated antibodies (ANA patterns, anti-Ro/SSA, anti-U1 RNP, etc.)
Laboratory platforms (immunoblot/EUROLINE, ELISA, immunoprecipitation) and interpretation caveats
Implications of specific antibodies for ILD risk, dysphagia and malignancy screening
Sensitivity, specificity and limitations of antibody testing

chapters.title: Muscle Biopsy in Myopathies: Indications and Histopathology
chapters.description: Principles of muscle biopsy, typical histologic and immunohistochemical findings in dermatomyositis and other myopathies, and differential features.
subtopics: Indications and techniques for muscle biopsy (open vs needle, site selection)
Histopathologic features of dermatomyositis (perifascicular atrophy, perimysial inflammation, capillary loss)
Complement and immunohistochemistry findings (C5b-9 deposition, MHC-I expression)
Findings in immune-mediated necrotising myopathy and inclusion body myositis
Interpretation pitfalls and correlation with clinical/imaging data

chapters.title: Nailfold Capillaroscopy and Cutaneous Microvascular Assessment
chapters.description: Use of nailfold capillaroscopy to evaluate microangiopathy in connective tissue disease and myositis, and interpretation of common abnormalities.
subtopics: Technique and normal capillaroscopic findings
Patterns seen in systemic sclerosis, dermatomyositis and other connective tissue diseases
Microhemorrhages, avascular areas, capillary dilation and dropout
Clinical utility in diagnosis, prognostication and monitoring

chapters.title: Imaging in Myositis and Neck Pathology: MRI, CT and PET
chapters.description: Role and interpretation of MRI for muscle inflammation, CT for neck and chest pathology, and FDG-PET in inflammatory myopathies and malignancy screening.
subtopics: MRI sequences and findings of active myositis (STIR/T2 hyperintensity, gadolinium enhancement) vs chronic atrophy/fibrosis

High-resolution CT chest for ILD patterns and pulmonary nodules
FDG-PET utility for identifying widespread muscle inflammation and occult malignancy
Limitations, artifacts and combining modalities for diagnosis

chapters.title: Pulmonary Manifestations of Myositis: Interstitial Lung Disease and Aspiration Pneumonitis
chapters.description: Spectrum of pulmonary involvement in inflammatory myopathies, including patterns of ILD, aspiration risk from bulbar weakness, and lung function testing interpretation.
subtopics: Types and radiologic patterns of myositis-associated ILD (NSIP, OP, UIP patterns)
Pathophysiology of aspiration pneumonitis vs aspiration pneumonia
Pulmonary function testing in restrictive vs obstructive disease and extrathoracic restriction
Clinical assessment and monitoring of respiratory muscle weakness
Management principles for ILD in connective tissue disease

chapters.title: Angioedema: Mechanisms, Types and Diagnostic Approach
chapters.description: Pathophysiology of angioedema (histamine-mediated, bradykinin-mediated, hereditary and acquired), clinical features and diagnostic testing.
subtopics: Mediators of angioedema: histamine vs bradykinin and implications for treatment
Hereditary angioedema (C1 inhibitor deficiency) and acquired C1-inhibitor dysfunction
Drug-induced angioedema (ACE inhibitors, DPP-4 inhibitors, NSAIDs)

Laboratory tests: C3/C4, C1 esterase inhibitor level and function, tryptase, complement activation markers
Emergency airway considerations and acute management

chapters.title: Infectious and Surgical Causes of Neck Swelling: Deep Neck Space Infections and Ludwig's Angina
chapters.description: Common infectious causes of neck swelling, their pathogenesis, clinical presentation and initial management principles.
subtopics: Etiology and pathogenesis of deep neck space infections (odontogenic, tonsillar, salivary)
Clinical signs and red flags of Ludwig's angina and retropharyngeal infections
Microbiology, sepsis considerations and indications for imaging and surgical drainage
Antimicrobial therapy choices and airway management strategies
Distinguishing infectious swelling from non-infectious causes

chapters.title: Differential Diagnosis of Subcutaneous and Cervical Edema
chapters.description: Systematic approach to causes of soft tissue swelling of the face and neck beyond angioedema, including vascular, infectious, inflammatory and neoplastic etiologies.
subtopics: Vascular causes (superior vena cava syndrome, venous thrombosis, congestive cardiac failure)
Inflammatory/autoimmune causes (dermatomyositis, lupus, vasculitis, urticarial vasculitis)
Infectious causes (cellulitis, sialadenitis, deep neck infections)
Neoplastic and obstructive causes (lymphadenopathy, salivary gland tumors, parapharyngeal masses)
Drug reactions, contact dermatitis and orofacial granulomatosis

chapters.title: Cancer Risk in Dermatomyositis: Epidemiology and Screening Strategies
chapters.description: Association between dermatomyositis and malignancy, risk stratification, and recommended screening approaches.
subtopics: Epidemiologic evidence linking dermatomyositis and specific cancers
Risk factors that increase likelihood of associated malignancy (age, certain autoantibodies, dysphagia, cutaneous features)
Baseline and interval screening strategies (imaging, tumor markers, endoscopic evaluations)
Role of PET-CT in occult cancer detection and limitations
Guidelines and consensus statements for myositis-associated cancer screening

chapters.title: Pharmacology and Therapeutic Management of Dermatomyositis and Other Inflammatory Myopathies
chapters.description: Evidence-based pharmacologic treatments for inflammatory myopathies, mechanisms of action, dosing strategies and monitoring.
subtopics: Glucocorticoids: mechanisms, pulse dosing, tapering strategies, adverse effects
Conventional steroid-sparing agents: methotrexate, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, tacrolimus (mechanisms, dosing, toxicities)
Biologic therapies: rituximab (anti-CD20), tofacitinib/JAK inhibitors and emerging agents
Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG): mechanisms, indications, dosing regimens and adverse effects
Treatment selection principles based on disease severity, organ involvement and comorbidities
Supportive care and rehabilitation (physiotherapy, nutritional support, speech/swallow therapy)

chapters.title: Immunosuppression: Infection Screening, Prophylaxis and Monitoring
chapters.description: Pre-treatment screening for latent and chronic infections, immunization considerations and prophylaxis strategies for patients receiving immunosuppressive therapy.
subtopics: Screening for latent tuberculosis (IGRA/TST) and HBV/HCV/HIV serologies
Viral serologies (VZV, CMV) and implications for management
Prophylaxis for opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis jirovecii prophylaxis options and indications)
Monitoring protocols for drug toxicities (CBC, LFTs, renal function, TPMT testing for azathioprine)
Vaccination recommendations before and during immunosuppression

chapters.title: Complications of Immunosuppressive Therapy: Recognition and Management
chapters.description: Common and serious adverse effects of agents used to treat myositis, and strategies to prevent and manage them.
subtopics: Hematologic toxicities (cytopenias, hemolytic anemia) and monitoring
Hepatotoxicity and nephrotoxicity with immunosuppressants
Infection risk and opportunistic infections (presentation and management)
Drug–drug interactions and peri-procedural considerations
Infusion-related reactions (IVIG, rituximab) and premedication strategies

chapters.title: Clinical Laboratory Interpretation in Autoimmune Myopathies
chapters.description: Interpretation of common laboratory tests in suspected inflammatory myopathies and autoimmune disease, including autoantibodies, inflammatory markers and muscle enzymes.
subtopics: Utility and limitations of ANA testing and ANA patterns

Acute phase reactants (CRP, ESR) and their meaning in inflammatory myopathies

chapters.title: Clinical Reasoning and Diagnostic Approach to Patients with Neck Swelling and Proximal Weakness
chapters.description: A framework for integrating history, exam, laboratory and imaging findings to approach patients presenting with neck swelling and muscle weakness.
subtopics: History-taking priorities: temporal course, systemic symptoms, medication exposures, preceding infections

Algorithmic use of laboratory tests (CK, autoantibodies, complement studies) and imaging to distinguish infectious, allergic and inflammatory causes

Risk stratification for airway compromise and indications for urgent intervention
